newsitem.title: UK: Newman Tonks gains after FKI bid.
newsitem.headline: Newman Tonks gains after FKI bid.

text.p: Shares in Newman Tonks Plc rose in early trading on Tuesday after engineering group FKI Plc launched a takeover bid for the maker of locks and door handles.
Newman shares were up 18-1/2p at 147-1/2 by 0812 GMT, extending a 27p rise on Monday.
The company said yesterday it had received an approach from FKI, but gave no details of the bid then.
FKI said its share-and-cash bid valued Newman at 150p per share and said there was a full cash alternative at 140p.
It said M&G and Britannic Assurance, holders of 13.4 percent of Newman shares, had pledged to accept the offer.

Traders said Newman Tonks shareholders were likely to welcome the offer after the stock's poor performance of the past year, in which it dropped from 119p at the end of 1995 to a closing low of 102p on October 17.

"1996 has been a year of misery for any holders of Newman Tonks and the stock has gone up in a straight line to the level of the bid," said one trader. "I would expect people are just going to say "thanks very much'."
By 0905 GMT FKI shares were down 3p at 197.
